Hi Hadley et al,

I'm working with a relatively complicated ddply operation, one that is
large enough that I want to use the (awesome!) progress bar. But the
progress bar gets to 100% only partially through the ddply call.
Looking at the code, it appears as if the progress bar applies only to
the llply() call, but not to the subsequent list_to_dataframe() call.
In this case, this step takes even longer than the llply step!

So... Is it expected that list_to_dataframe would take so long? If
not, under what circumstances would it? If so, consider "make progress
bar apply to list_to_dataframe" an enhancement request. :)

Thanks!

 -Harlan

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm not sure why you would not want to keep those data.frames in a
list, but if you insist on having them as separate objects in the
global environment you could use ?assign,

data1 <- data.frame(a=1:10, b=letters[1:10])
data2 <- data.frame(a=rnorm(10), b=LETTERS[1:10])

datalist<-list(data1,data2)
datalist <- llply(datalist, transform, c=a^2)

names(datalist) <- paste("data", 1:2, sep="")

l_ply(seq_along(datalist), function(l)
      assign(names(datalist[l]), datalist[[l]], pos=1) )

HTH,

baptiste

Hi everyone,

I want to apply a function to each column of a data.frame and get a
data.frame as result. If I was doing this on different subsets of the
data.frame, I would do:

data <- data.frame(a=runif(10), b=rnorm(10), c=rep(c(1,2), each=5))

ddply(data, ~c, colwise(function(x){mean(x)+sd(x)}))

but here I want to use *all* lines of the data.frame. So I ended up doing:

data <- data[,-3]
colwise(function(x){mean(x)+sd(x)})(data)

but it "feels" wrong. Is there a more natural way (even in plain R,
not necessarily plyr)? It looks like I want sapply but which returns a
data.frame. as.data.frame(sapply(...)) transposes the data.frame, just
as ldply does and I don't want that.

Thanks in advance. Sincerely,

JiHO
